newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian copper slide continues, other metals steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian copper slide continues, other metals steady.

text.p: Copper prices extended losses while other base metals were steady on the local market, dealers said.
Overall sentiment remained subdued amid poor buying enquiries from the industrial consumers as well as reports of losses in the world market.

Ready copper slid a further 50 rupees to 13,500 rupees per quintal, after dropping 100 rupees on Saturday. Zinc was quiet at 7,850 rupees, as was lead at 4,350 rupees per quintal but undertone was weak.
Zinc fell 50 rupees and lead was down 200 rupees per quintal on Saturday.

"Earlier in the last week metals were firm on expectation that state-owned producers may hike prices but on the contrary these producers have reduced prices for current month which in turn led to setback in the prices," said Sharad Parikh president of Bombay Metal Exchange.
"Hindustan Copper had reduced prices by 1,000/2,000 rupees per tonnes while Hindustan Zinc had reduced prices of zinc by 1,000 rupees per tonne and lead by 4,000 rupees per tonne," he said.

Tin was steady at 31,200 rupees after losing 300 rupees on Saturday while nickel was quiet at 36,100 rupees per quintal after falling 300 rupees on Saturday. Aluminium was indicated unchanged at 7,450 rupees per quintal amid nominal activity.
